# `md/link-image-reference-definitions`

**Every reference definition is used, and defined once**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-data` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-data` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | Markdown |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:md/recommended` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `ignored_definitions` |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.1.0 |
| **Ported from** | `markdownlint/MD053` |

## What it checks

A `[label]: url` definition is referred to by some link or image, and no label is defined twice. The fix deletes the unused or repeated definition.

**Why:** A definition nothing uses is dead text that goes stale, and only the first of two definitions counts, so the second one misleads.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-data
pip install codelaw-rules-data
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:md/recommended` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:md/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"md/link-image-reference-definitions" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignored_definitions` | `string[]` | `["//"]` | labels never reported (`[//]: # (…)` is a comment idiom) |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."md/link-image-reference-definitions"]
severity = "error"

[rules."md/link-image-reference-definitions".options]
ignored_definitions = ["//"]
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"md/link-image-reference-definitions" = { severity = "error", options = { ignored_definitions = ["//"] } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `ignored_definitions`

*string[]* · default `["//"]`

labels never reported (`[//]: # (…)` is a comment idiom)

```toml
[rules."md/link-image-reference-definitions".options]
ignored_definitions = ["//"]
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.md"]
rules = { "md/link-image-reference-definitions" = { options = { ignored_definitions = ["//"] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.md"]
rules = { "md/link-image-reference-definitions" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"md/link-image-reference-definitions" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"md/link-image-reference-definitions" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"md/link-image-reference-definitions" = { severity = "warn", options = { ignored_definitions = ["//"] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "md/link-image-reference-definitions": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"ignored_definitions": ["//"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **Markdown:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore md/link-image-reference-definitions: <reason> -->`
- **Dated:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore md/link-image-reference-definitions expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason> -->`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule md/link-image-reference-definitions --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain md/link-image-reference-definitions       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule md/link-image-reference-definitions  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                       # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### Markdown

#### Don't

````md
Read [the spec][spec].

[spec]: https://spec.commonmark.org/
[old]: https://example.com/old
````

#### Do

````md
Read [the spec][spec].

[spec]: https://spec.commonmark.org/
````
